section: Andhra in the freedom movement - Alluri Sitarama Raju and the Rampa Rebellion, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
subsections: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb
Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born at which of the following places?
accepted.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born on 4 July 1897 at Pandrangi, also referred to as Pandarangipeta, near Vizianagaram. Mogallu was his ancestral village.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the birthplace from the ancestral village and later places associated with the leader.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alluri Sitarama Raju:
1. His ancestral village was Mogallu in West Godavari.
2. He was popularly known by the nickname Chittibabu.
3. Erramalli Narasimha Rao wrote his biography.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mogallu was his ancestral village, Chittibabu was his nickname, and Erramalli Narasimha Rao was his biographer.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related identity details and verify each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: The Rampa or Manyam Rebellion was principally based in which area?
o: The Gudem hills of the East Godavari Agency
accepted.x: The rebellion was based in the Gudem hills, located in the Agency area of East Godavari.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue to separate the rebellion's operational area from other hill regions of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a cause of the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Introduction of permanent settlement in the Gudem hills
Oppressive functioning of the Muttadari system
Loss of forest and podu rights under the Madras Forest Act
accepted.x: The rebellion was caused by restrictions on forest and podu rights, begar for road building and the oppressive Muttadari system, along with the actions of Tahsildar Bastian. Permanent settlement was not identified as a cause.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated cluster of causes.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: The Madras Forest Act associated with the Rampa Rebellion was enacted in:
accepted.x: The tribal grievances were intensified by the Madras Forest Act of 1882, which restricted traditional forest and podu rights.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced year options by linking the date to the specific colonial forest measure.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Alluri Sitarama Raju is correct?
1. He visited Chittagong in 1921 to meet Bengali revolutionaries.
2. He respected Gandhi but believed that force was necessary.
3. He was formally affiliated to the Indian National Congress.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. He visited Chittagong in 1921, respected Gandhi and believed in the necessity of force, but he was not affiliated with the Congress.
accepted.tq: Use the affiliation statement as the trap while retaining the two correct ideological details.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju in chronological order:
A. Visit to Chittagong to meet Bengali revolutionaries
B. Establishment of his hut near Krishnadevipeta
C. First raid on the Chintapalli police station
D. Capture and shooting at Koyyuru
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: His hut near Krishnadevipeta dates to 1919, the Chittagong visit to 1921, the Chintapalli raid to 22 August 1922, and his death to 7 May 1924.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate events by year.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: After the raid on Chintapalli, which sequence correctly represents the subsequent police-station raids associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju?
accepted.x: After the first raid at Chintapalli, the subsequent raids mentioned were at Krishnadevipeta, Rajavommangi and Addateegala.
accepted.tq: Track the sequence of related raids rather than confusing the first raid with later actions.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Scott and Coward — killed in an ambush
Kanchu Meenan and Goodall — leaders of the Ramadandu
Bastian and Erramalli — commanders of the Malabar Special Police
Mallu Dora and Gantam Dora — British officers killed at Chintapalli
accepted.x: British officers Scott and Coward were killed in an ambush during the rebellion. Kanchu Meenan captured Raju, Goodall was present at his shooting, and Mallu Dora and Gantam Dora were his lieutenants.
accepted.tq: Match persons with their precise roles and reject swapped identities.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the first raid on the Chintapalli police station was to:
accepted.x: The first raid, on 22 August 1922, was undertaken to seize arms from the police station.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate operational objective rather than a broader cause of the rebellion.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: The Rampa Rebellion was brought to an end when Alluri Sitarama Raju was captured and shot at:
accepted.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was captured and shot on 7 May 1924 at Koyyuru. His tomb is at Krishnadevipeta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the place of death from the place of the tomb and the site of the direct battle.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: Who captured Alluri Sitarama Raju before his execution in May 1924?
accepted.x: Jamadar Kanchu Meenan captured Alluri Sitarama Raju. He was subsequently shot on 7 May 1924 before Major Goodall.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the captor from the officer present at the execution and from earlier British officials.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the end of the Rampa Rebellion:
1. Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot on 7 May 1924.
2. His last rites were performed on 8 May 1924.
3. The last rites took place near the Tandava river at Krishnadevipeta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. He was shot on 7 May 1924, and his last rites were performed the following day at Krishnadevipeta near the Tandava river.
accepted.tq: Test adjacent dates and the location of the final rites as separate statements.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: Which forces were employed by the British to suppress the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Punjab Police and Central Reserve Police
Malabar Special Police and Assam Rifles
accepted.x: The British crackdown involved the Malabar Special Police and the Assam Rifles.
accepted.tq: Match the historical event with the specific forces used in the crackdown.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Rampa Rebellion?
o: It was confined to the coastal municipalities of Guntur district.
It troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement did.
It was affiliated formally with the Indian National Congress and led through Congress committees.
It ended immediately after the imposition of the Madras Forest Act.
accepted.x: The rebellion troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement. It was an armed tribal rebellion in the Agency area and was not formally affiliated with the Congress.
accepted.tq: Select the precise comparative statement while rejecting exaggerated organisational and geographical claims.
accepted.sec: Alluri Sitarama Raju - birthplace, Rampa, raids, title, battles, death, tomb

accepted.s: The Chirala-Perala Satyagraha arose primarily because:
o: The British prohibited the Ramadandu from holding public meetings.
The villages were brought under the Forest Act and denied podu rights.
The two villages were converted into a municipality and their annual tax burden increased sharply.
The residents were forced to migrate to the Gudem hills.
accepted.x: Chirala and Perala were made a municipality, and the annual tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000, provoking the movement.
accepted.tq: Match the movement with its immediate administrative and fiscal trigger.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: The annual tax imposed on Chirala and Perala increased from approximately:
accepted.x: After municipalisation, the annual tax increased from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000.
accepted.tq: Compare the starting and final values rather than selecting a distractor with a reversed or reduced increase.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement:
1. Chirala and Perala were in Bapatla taluk.
2. The affected population was approximately 15,000.
3. The residents left the municipal limits and settled at Ramnagar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The villages were in Bapatla taluk, had a population of about 15,000, and many residents moved to Ramnagar outside the municipal limits.
accepted.tq: Combine location, scale and action into a single movement-based statement question.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: The exodus of Chirala-Perala residents to Ramnagar took place on:
accepted.x: At midnight on 25 April 1921, the residents began their exodus to the new camp at Ramnagar.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the mass exodus from the later date of Duggirala's arrest.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: How many residents are specifically recorded as having left Chirala and Perala for Ramnagar?
accepted.x: A total of 13,572 out of 15,326 residents left for the Ramnagar camp outside the municipal limits.
accepted.tq: Separate the number who migrated from the total population figure.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Which of the following arrangements best describes the settlement established by the Chirala-Perala residents at Ramnagar?
o: A parallel assembly and an arbitration court
A municipal council and a police station
A military camp and a revenue court
A legislative council and a permanent civil court
accepted.x: The Ramnagar settlement maintained a parallel all-caste assembly and an arbitration court outside the municipal limits.
accepted.tq: Match the protest settlement with its distinctive parallel institutions.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: The Ramnagar settlement established during the Chirala-Perala movement lasted for approximately:
accepted.x: The settlement at Ramnagar continued for about 11 months before the movement collapsed and the people returned.
accepted.tq: Use the duration as the distinguishing numerical fact among closely related periods.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was arrested on 1 October 1921 primarily because he:
o: Broke a ban on public speaking after his Berhampur speech
Organised an armed raid in the Gudem hills
Refused to pay the municipal tax
accepted.x: After his Berhampur speech, Duggirala was prohibited from speaking for two months. He defied the ban and was arrested on 1 October 1921.
accepted.tq: Link the arrest to the specific act that violated the colonial order.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was sentenced to imprisonment for:
accepted.x: He was tried and sentenced to one year in prison after defying the prohibition on his public speaking.
accepted.tq: Test the exact punishment rather than confusing it with imprisonment terms of other freedom fighters.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Who was the first woman jailed in connection with the Chirala-Perala movement?
accepted.x: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was recorded as the first woman jailed in connection with the movement. Twelve women were arrested in all.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first woman prisoner from another woman activist associated with the movement.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT mentioned as a reason for the failure of the Chirala-Perala movement?
o: Withdrawal of support by the Ramadandu volunteers after an armed defeat
accepted.x: The movement weakened because of lack of funds, jealousy among other Congress leaders and the absence of second-line leaders. An armed defeat of the Ramadandu was not given as a cause.
accepted.tq: Identify the invented organisational explanation among the actual reasons for failure.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: The municipality of Chirala and Perala was abolished in 1938 during the ministry of:
o: Rajagopalachari, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
Tanguturi Prakasam, with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya as minister concerned
P. Subbarayan, with Konda Venkatappayya as minister concerned
Bobbili Raja, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
accepted.x: The municipality was abolished in 1938 during the Rajaji ministry, when Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Local Self-Government Minister.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative outcome with the correct ministry and minister instead of swapping office-holders.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Who founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala?
accepted.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its founder while avoiding confusion with other Andhra leaders.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: The book *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by:
accepted.x: *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by Pisapati Narayana Sastri.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work association and reject names linked with other events in the same region.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi described the Chirala-Perala municipality in *Young India* as an institution that mainly meant:
accepted.x: Gandhi wrote in *Young India* that the municipality only meant more taxes for the people of Chirala and Perala.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise contemporary characterisation rather than a general description of municipal reform.
accepted.sec: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya - Chirala-Perala, Ramadandu, Andhra Ratna

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
accepted.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the Chirala-Perala movement. Ramadandu was his volunteer corps, while the other pairings assign unrelated roles or works.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure leader–movement pair and eliminate swapped associations.
